# The Stars That Blaze and Fade

## Scripture
*"You are a mist that appears for a little while and then vanishes."* — James 4:14 (NIV)

## Reflection
On a clear November night, if you're patient and away from city lights, you might catch a Leonid meteor streaking across the sky. The Leonid shower peaks each year around mid-November, and on rare occasions it erupts into a dazzling storm of hundreds or thousands of meteors per hour. But most years? Just a few quiet trails per hour—brief flashes of light that blaze and vanish in a heartbeat.

Meteors remind us of something the apostle James wrote plainly: our lives are mists, appearing for a little while and then vanishing. It sounds sobering, even somber. But consider the meteor—it doesn't mourn its brevity. It simply shines, bright and faithful, for the moment it was given.

November's skies are teaching us something about time. The harvest is past, the days are shortening, and we're reminded that seasons don't last forever. Yet our briefness isn't cause for despair—it's a call to presence. To burn with the light we've been given, right where God has placed us, for however long the sky grants us.

The God who set the Leonids in motion, repeating their faithful display year after year for millennia, is the same God who holds your fleeting days with eternal purpose. You may be a mist—but you are a mist He knows by name.

## Prayer
Father, our days are brief, yet You are eternal. Help us shine faithfully in the time we're given—not grasping at permanence, but trusting Your purpose in every fleeting moment. Amen.
